score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current HSE/GOV.UK/legislation readback, explicit consultation-zone and development-sensitivity handling, and prevention of proximity to a major hazard being converted into automatic refusal, approval or parcel risk score.

sources.label: GOV.UK hazardous substances planning guidance
sources.fact: Hazardous substances consent controls specified substances at/above controlled quantities and is separate from planning permission and environmental permitting.

sources.label: HSE hazardous substance consent
sources.fact: HSE is a statutory consultee; consent decisions are made by the hazardous substances authority and HSE risk zones inform later relevant planning consultations.

sources.label: HSE land-use planning role
sources.fact: Current HSE page confirms consultation distances around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines and HSE advisory role for relevant development.

sources.label: HSE Planning Advice Web App
sources.fact: The Web App uses inner/middle/outer consultation zones plus development type, size and intensity to provide advise-against/not-advise-against planning advice.

sources.label: HSE land-use planning methodology
sources.fact: Advice combines consultation zone and development sensitivity level; major accident hazard pipelines can require pipeline-specific reconsideration where protection differs locally.

sources.label: HSE developer planning advice
sources.fact: Developers can check whether a plot lies within a consultation zone and obtain pre-application advice; a zone hit alone is not HSE's final advice for an unmodelled proposal.

sources.label: HSE LUP resources
sources.fact: HSE resources describe statutory consultation around hazardous installations and major accident hazard pipelines and use of the Planning Advice Web App.

sources.label: HSE planning call-in policy
sources.fact: If an authority proposes to grant contrary to HSE advice within a major-hazard consultation zone, HSE may consider requesting call-in; this is case-specific, not automatic.

sources.label: HSE hazardous substance consent smart forms
sources.fact: Current HSE smart-form service supports applications/variations/continuation of consent and confirms consent is required above controlled quantities.

sources.label: Planning (Hazardous Substances) Act 1990
sources.fact: Primary legislation provides the hazardous-substances consent framework and powers to prescribe substances and controlled quantities.

sources.label: Planning (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2015
sources.fact: 2015 Regulations specify controlled quantities, application/publicity and related procedures; quantity and substance evidence is required.

sources.label: Control of Major Accident Hazards Regulations 2015
sources.fact: COMAH safety-management controls are distinct from the land-use planning hazardous-substances consent regime; one regime is not treated as proof of compliance with the other.

examples.result: A candidate inside an HSE consultation distance is not automatically rejected; actual zone, development sensitivity and HSE advice are required.
A hazardous-substances consent near a parcel is not itself evidence that the parcel is unsafe or undevelopable.
Absence of a public HSE Web App result is not treated as no major-hazard constraint; exact coordinates and current consultation-zone check are required.
Pipeline proximity is not converted to a fixed exclusion buffer; HSE methodology and pipeline protection can be location-specific.
HSE advise-against/not-advise-against is not inferred without an actual proposal type/size/intensity or authoritative consultation response.
Hazardous substances consent is kept separate from planning permission, COMAH duties and environmental permits.
Call-in is not presumed merely because HSE advice may be adverse; the authority decision and HSE call-in assessment must be evidenced.
No major-hazard promotion/demotion occurs without exact site geometry, current HSE zone/advice and proposal sensitivity binding.
